forces.title: Prolonged Contraction & Weak Demand in Construction
forces.description: The UK construction sector faces a sustained and accelerating contraction (3.3% forecast for 2026), driven by weak demand, weakening confidence, and subdued private investment. This broad market downturn, reflected in persistent low PMI scores, directly reduces tender activity and project opportunities for EPC firms, particularly impacting commercial and residential segments, making the overall operating environment highly challenging.

forces.title: Robust Demand for Critical National Infrastructure & Strategic Projects
forces.description: The UK is experiencing robust demand for critical national infrastructure, including energy, water, utilities, telecoms, and data centres, alongside strategic projects in defence and industrial sectors. This sustained public and private investment provides a significant and diverse project pipeline for Engineering, Procurement & Construction (EPC) firms, driving opportunities for large-scale design, build, and handover contracts and acting as a crucial counterweight to weaknesses in other construction segments.
forces.source_title: Agents' summary of business conditions - June 2026

forces.title: Elevated Insolvencies & Financial Strain Across Construction
forces.description: Insolvency levels in the construction sector remain elevated, accounting for ~17% of all UK corporate insolvencies, with financial stress spreading to mid-sized and established main contractors and specialist subcontractors. This pervasive financial fragility in the supply chain and among counterparties creates significant credit risk for EPC firms, threatening project stability, increasing the likelihood of payment delays, and demanding rigorous financial assessment of partners and subcontractors.

forces.title: Tightened Funding & High Borrowing Costs
forces.description: Funding conditions for the construction sector have tightened, with high borrowing costs and increased selectivity from lenders, making finance less accessible for smaller firms and those with weaker track records. This directly impacts capital-intensive EPC firms by increasing the cost of capital, limiting investment capacity, and hindering their ability to secure and execute large projects, particularly in a subdued demand environment.
forces.source_title: Agents' summary of business conditions - September 2026

forces.title: Geopolitical Conflict & Supply Chain Disruptions
forces.description: The Middle East conflict has introduced significant geopolitical uncertainty, impacting demand, supply chains, and input costs across sectors. This has led to sharp declines in demand for UK construction services exports to the region, and risks disrupting global shipping, causing increased freight costs and extended delivery times for materials. For EPC firms, this creates project delays, cost overruns, and erosion of confidence.
forces.source_title: Agents' summary of business conditions - April 2026

forces.title: Planning & Regulatory Constraints Delay Projects
forces.description: Persistent planning and regulatory delays remain a strong constraint on new construction, significantly extending project timelines, increasing costs, and challenging viability. While government initiatives aim to ease this regime, the current environment means EPC firms face operational and financial risks, including tied-up working capital and potential disputes, hindering efficient project delivery and undermining the realization of pipeline opportunities.
forces.source_title: Agents' summary of business conditions - March 2026

forces.title: Uncertain & Underperforming Government Infrastructure Spending
forces.description: Public sector spending on infrastructure is reported to be flat and lower than expected, with contacts citing uncertainty or slowness in government funding conversion to project starts. This underperformance and unpredictability create significant revenue uncertainty and cash flow management issues for EPC firms heavily reliant on public contracts, undermining the anticipated tailwind from government investment and delaying project actualization.
forces.source_title: Agents' summary of business conditions - April 2026

forces.title: Defence Sector Shift to Resilience-Led Industrial Models
forces.description: The UK defence sector is undergoing a profound structural shift from efficiency-led to resilience-led industrial models, driven by geopolitical realities. This necessitates deliberate, long-term investment in infrastructure and workforce capabilities across the defence industrial base to ensure 'just-in-case' capacity. For EPC firms, this creates sustained, strategic demand for large-scale, robust defence infrastructure and industrial facilities, representing a high-impact, long-term opportunity.

forces.title: Cooling Demand for Industrial & Commercial Real Estate
forces.description: Demand for industrial space is cooling, and many new commercial office and care home schemes are no longer viable due to elevated costs and market uncertainties. This directly reduces a significant end-market for Engineering, Procurement & Construction (EPC) firms involved in large-scale building works, limiting new contract opportunities and intensifying competition for remaining projects, contributing to overall market weakness.
forces.source_title: Agents' summary of business conditions - April 2026

forces.title: Regulatory Burden from New Trade Policies & Quotas
forces.description: New regulatory burdens, such as the EU's Carbon Border Adjustment Mechanism (CBAM) and new steel import quotas (both EU and UK), are expected to significantly disrupt goods exports to the EU and increase material costs. For EPC firms, particularly those sourcing materials internationally or involved in projects with cross-border material flows, these policies introduce higher compliance costs, material price increases, and supply chain complexities, negatively impacting project budgets and stability.
forces.source_title: Agents' summary of business conditions - April 2026

forces.title: Productivity Gains from Automation and AI Adoption
forces.description: Many organizations are leveraging automation and AI-enabled productivity gains to meet demand without additional hiring, with estimated time savings ranging from 5% to 70% for specific tasks. For Engineering, Procurement & Construction (EPC) firms, this presents a significant opportunity to reduce labour costs, optimize design processes, enhance project management, and increase operational efficiency, thereby contributing to improved project profitability and overall competitiveness.
forces.source_title: Agents' summary of business conditions - March 2026

forces.title: Increased Fixed Costs from Business Rates
forces.description: Businesses across the UK are facing increased fixed costs this year due to rises in business rates. For Engineering, Procurement & Construction (EPC) firms, these higher operational overheads add to the financial burden, further compressing profit margins. This pressure is particularly acute in a market characterized by subdued demand and limited pricing power, necessitating greater operational efficiency to maintain profitability.
forces.source_title: Agents' summary of business conditions - March 2026

forces.title: Slower-Than-Expected Infrastructure Spending Momentum
forces.description: While infrastructure spending is increasing, its pace is slower than initially anticipated by contacts, and pipelines are slow to convert into project starts. This means a deferred realization of potential tailwinds for EPC firms, creating a more challenging near-term operating environment despite long-term demand. The slower momentum contributes to overall market uncertainty and can impact cash flow and project scheduling.
forces.source_title: Agents' summary of business conditions - September 2026

viewpoints.title: UK construction outlook weakened by rising costs and subdued investment
viewpoints.description: The UK construction sector is forecast to contract by 3.3% in 2026, a downgrade from earlier predictions, primarily due to weakening confidence, rising financing and construction costs, and reduced project viability. Insolvencies remain elevated, affecting not just SMEs but also mid-sized and established main contractors and specialist subcontractors. While infrastructure is a resilient subsector, the overall market remains challenging with demand still below expansion levels. EPC firms, as main contractors, face significant financial stress across their supply chains.

viewpoints.title: UK construction remains weak despite strong infrastructure pipeline
viewpoints.description: The UK construction sector continues to experience weakness, particularly in housebuilding, with heightened uncertainty and ongoing cost pressures delaying projects and depressing confidence. Although there is a substantial pipeline of public and private infrastructure work, including nuclear, energy, utilities, and defence, concerns persist regarding project delivery due to planning and regulatory constraints. This suggests a challenging environment for EPC firms, where potential long-term opportunities are hampered by near-term operational hurdles and funding conditions.
viewpoints.source_title: Agents' summary of business conditions - September 2026

viewpoints.title: UK construction output falling, but industrial and infrastructure pipelines strong
viewpoints.description: UK construction output continues to fall modestly, driven by elevated geopolitical uncertainty and rising cost pressures, which have reduced confidence and slowed decision-making. While residential and commercial projects face viability challenges, public sector demand remains steady, and industrial activity continues to grow. Strong pipelines for public sector, defence, and major infrastructure spend offer potential upside for EPC firms, though concerns exist that these projects may be slow to materialize due to political uncertainty and steel quotas.
viewpoints.source_title: Agents' summary of business conditions - July 2026

viewpoints.title: Construction output falling, but infrastructure projects remain busy
viewpoints.description: UK construction activity continues its modest decline year-on-year, driven by soft demand, rising costs, and heightened uncertainty. However, infrastructure contractors remain busy with large projects in energy, water, telecoms, and data centres, reporting a reasonable pipeline of work. Despite this, overall confidence is down, partly due to domestic political uncertainty potentially weighing on public spending and firms building stocks against supply disruption. This presents a mixed outlook for EPC, with resilient demand in specific infrastructure segments offset by broader market headwinds.
viewpoints.source_title: Agents' summary of business conditions - June 2026

viewpoints.title: Construction sector faces prolonged contraction and elevated insolvencies
viewpoints.description: The UK construction sector continues its prolonged contraction, with the S&P Global UK Construction PMI falling to 39.7 in April 2026, marking 16 consecutive months of decline. This is attributed to softer demand, geopolitical uncertainty from the Middle East conflict, and rising energy costs, leading to project delays and reduced tender activity. The sector is forecast to contract by 2.5% in 2026, with persistent elevated insolvency levels, affecting approximately 17% of all UK firms. For EPC, while infrastructure shows resilience, the overall environment remains highly challenging.

viewpoints.title: Middle East conflict erodes construction confidence, delays recovery
viewpoints.description: The Middle East conflict has significantly eroded business confidence, with contacts expressing worries about its potential impact on demand, supply chains, and input costs, particularly for the construction sector. While direct impacts on output are not yet widespread, the overall annual output growth remains weak, dragged down by declining activity in construction. This geopolitical event jeopardizes the anticipated modest recovery in profit margins for EPC firms, creating an environment of heightened uncertainty and cost pressure.
viewpoints.source_title: Agents' summary of business conditions - April 2026

viewpoints.title: Public infrastructure spending flat amid declining construction output
viewpoints.description: UK construction output continues its annual decline, primarily due to weak demand and elevated costs. While residential and commercial construction remain weak, public sector spending on infrastructure is currently flat and performing below expectations. This represents a significant headwind for Engineering, Procurement & Construction (EPC) firms, who rely heavily on government-backed infrastructure projects. The lack of anticipated growth in public spending further dampens confidence in the sector amidst ongoing challenges.
viewpoints.source_title: Agents' summary of business conditions - April 2026

viewpoints.title: Construction recovery pushed to 2027 amid downbeat outlook
viewpoints.description: Construction contacts have become more downbeat about the sector's prospects, with expectations for recovery now pushed out to 2027. This reflects a lacklustre overall economic picture and cautious expectations for real activity, with little evidence of consumer spending rallying. For Engineering, Procurement & Construction (EPC) firms, this indicates a prolonged period of challenging market conditions, requiring continued resilience and strategic adaptation to navigate delayed recovery timelines.
viewpoints.source_title: Agents' summary of business conditions - March 2026

viewpoints.title: Construction output decline accelerates, recovery delayed to 2027
viewpoints.description: The decline in UK construction output has accelerated year-on-year, driven by weak demand, high build costs, uncertain government funding, limited access to finance, and ongoing planning and regulatory delays. While infrastructure activity shows modest positivity with growth in energy and industrial projects, pipelines are slow to convert into starts. This reinforces a downbeat outlook for Engineering, Procurement & Construction (EPC) firms, with recovery expectations for construction-linked activity now pushed out to late 2026 or early 2027.
viewpoints.source_title: Agents' summary of business conditions - March 2026

pnl_drivers.description: Materials such as plastics, petrochemical derivatives, and some metals are seeing double-digit price increases, dependent on energy prices and geopolitical factors. For EPC firms, these are direct input costs that significantly impact project budgets and profitability, necessitating careful procurement and cost management strategies.

pnl_drivers.driver: Energy and labour intensive input costs
pnl_drivers.description: Output price inflation for domestic manufacturers is higher in sectors with energy or UK labour intensive inputs. EPC projects are typically both, meaning higher costs for materials and labour directly translate to increased project expenses, potentially compressing profit margins if not fully passed on to clients.

pnl_drivers.driver: Ability to pass on costs and efficiency savings
pnl_drivers.description: While profit margins remain under pressure, some firms are managing to reduce compression by finding efficiency savings and passing on a portion of increased costs through price adjustments. EPC firms need to leverage efficiency gains and negotiate contractual clauses (like escalators) to mitigate the impact of rising input costs on project profitability.

pnl_drivers.driver: Supply chain constraints and extended delivery times
pnl_drivers.description: Constraints in supply chains are contributing to cost pressures, particularly across energy infrastructure and construction, leading to extended delivery times. For EPC firms, this directly increases project durations and costs, impacting project schedules and potentially incurring penalties, thereby negatively affecting overall project profitability and working capital.

Contacts are increasingly concerned about the impact of higher-than-expected inflation on 2027 pay settlements, potentially slowing wage disinflation. For Engineering, Procurement & Construction (EPC) firms, labour costs are a significant component of project expenses. Increased wage pressure will elevate operational costs, challenging project budgets and potentially impacting overall profitability if not managed through pricing or efficiency gains.

pnl_drivers.driver: Surge in fuel prices and transport costs due to ME conflict
pnl_drivers.description: The Middle East conflict has caused an immediate surge in fuel prices, leading to higher costs for transported goods and alternative routing of imports, which increases both cost and delivery times. For Engineering, Procurement & Construction (EPC) firms, this directly raises logistics expenses for materials and equipment, impacting project budgets and potentially causing delays, thereby compressing profit margins.

pnl_drivers.driver: Elevated energy costs for industrial transition
pnl_drivers.description: High energy costs continue to weigh on industrial sectors, exacerbated by the Middle East conflict. The cost of industrial transition, including decarbonisation and electrification efforts, also adds financial burden. EPC firms undertaking such projects face increased operational expenses and input costs, which, combined with elevated financing conditions, reduce overall project profitability.

The construction sector continues to experience elevated financial stress, driven by weak demand and tight margins. For EPC firms, this increases the risk of payment delays from clients and insolvency among subcontractors, directly impacting cash flow and project profitability, and potentially leading to project disruptions.

pnl_drivers.driver: Disruption to global shipping lines and increased transport costs
pnl_drivers.description: The Middle East conflict poses a risk of disrupting global shipping lines, not just to and from the Gulf, leading to very sharp rises in transport costs. For EPC firms, this directly impacts the cost of importing materials and equipment, increasing project logistics expenses and potentially causing delays, thereby compressing profit margins.

pnl_drivers.driver: EU Carbon Border Adjustment Mechanism (CBAM) and new steel quotas
pnl_drivers.description: The EU's CBAM (effective January 2026, UK from January 2027) and new EU steel quotas are expected to significantly disrupt goods exports to the EU. For EPC firms, particularly those relying on imported steel or other covered materials from the EU or exporting components to the EU, these measures will increase compliance costs and material prices, negatively impacting project budgets and supply chain stability.

pnl_drivers.driver: Rising materials cost inflation from oil, energy, and metals
pnl_drivers.description: Materials cost inflation has increased significantly, primarily driven by rising oil and energy prices, alongside spikes in some metals prices. These elevated raw material costs will intensify the squeeze on profit margins for EPC firms, as they directly impact procurement budgets for large-scale projects and are expected to feed through to products like plastics and fertilizers.

Profit margins are expected to intensify, reversing earlier expectations of a lessening squeeze. While some cost increases can be passed through via fuel escalators or indexation clauses, and customers may accept higher prices for essential material inputs, EPC firms fear that passing through other cost pressures will become more difficult due to clients facing their own inflation and interest rate challenges, leading to cautious pricing strategies.

pnl_drivers.driver: Increased prevalence of escalator clauses for cost pass-through
pnl_drivers.description: The increased prevalence of escalator clauses in contracts, particularly post-Ukraine, is enabling quicker pass-through of fuel and metal surcharges. For Engineering, Procurement & Construction (EPC) firms, these clauses are a vital mechanism to mitigate the impact of rising input costs, allowing them to adjust pricing in response to volatile energy and material markets, thereby protecting profit margins more effectively.

pnl_drivers.driver: Higher hedging prices for oil and gas output for 2027
pnl_drivers.description: Producers of oil and gas are hedging their 2027 output at higher prices, indicating elevated energy costs for the future. For EPC firms, this suggests continued high operational costs related to energy-intensive processes and equipment, impacting long-term project budgeting and profitability. This necessitates strategic energy procurement and risk management to control future project expenses.

pnl_drivers.driver: Modest material cost inflation and lower imported goods inflation
pnl_drivers.description: As of March 2026, material cost inflation remained modest, with imported finished goods inflation also low, supported by factors like lower freight costs and exchange rate moves. For EPC firms, this temporary easing of input costs offered some relief from pressure, although the ability to pass on costs remained limited due to subdued demand and client pushback on pricing.

pnl_drivers.driver: Squeezed profit margins due to subdued demand and limited pricing power
pnl_drivers.description: Profit margins for businesses, including those in construction-linked sectors, remained squeezed. Subdued demand limited firms' ability to pass on higher costs, preventing a substantive recovery. This pressure on pricing power for EPC firms means they must absorb cost increases or find efficiencies, impacting overall project profitability in a competitive environment.

pnl_drivers.driver: Increased fixed costs from business rates increases
pnl_drivers.description: Businesses are facing increased fixed costs this year due to rises in business rates. For Engineering, Procurement & Construction (EPC) firms, these higher overheads add to the financial burden, further compressing profit margins and necessitating greater operational efficiency to maintain profitability, especially when demand is subdued and pricing power is limited.

market_sizing.methodology: Analysis of cost pressures, pricing power, and financial health impacting profitability in the UK construction and manufacturing sectors, with specific attention to material, energy, and labour inputs, and the impact of geopolitical and regulatory factors.
market_sizing.source_title: Agents' summary of business conditions - September 2026
